text:
nina: Following the postmortem, let's capture clear owners + finish dates for the GPU capacity/autoscale remediation. Keep items minimal and verifiable.
raphael: I'll take a pass at the autoscale circuit-breaker and the emergency override flow. Target Weds EOD.
tom: I'll pick up scheduler watermarks and preemption tuning. I ran a quick test that suggests lowering preempt threshold to 0.18 reduces tail evictions but might increase short spikes. Need canary.
zoe: I'll own the customer communications + JIRA epic linking. Also will draft the outbound for impacted enterprise customers.
nina: Nice. Quick proposed task list:
- RAPHAEL: autoscale circuit-breaker -> design doc + helm values by 2026-04-06
- TOM: scheduler watermarks & preemption -> PR + canary plan by 2026-04-07
- ZOE: comms + epic -> confluence draft + JIRA epic created by 2026-04-05
- NINA: runbook updates -> include experiment rollback steps + post-change checklist by 2026-04-08
- OPS-BOT / infra: short-lived capacity override for load test -> schedule 2026-04-09 08:00-10:00 UTC
raphael: Design note: circuit-breaker will watch cluster CPU/GPU headroom + 95th queue depth. If queue depth spikes > X for 2m, trigger scale up and enable fallback routing. Will post spec.
tom: Canary approach: 1% of traffic for 2h -> 5% for 6h -> 20% for 24h. Rollback command: 
```
kubectl patch configmap scheduler --patch '{"data":{"preempt_threshold":"0.18"}}'
# rollback
kubectl patch configmap scheduler --patch '{"data":{"preempt_threshold":"0.25"}}'
```
zoe: I'll coordinate with CS on a soft notice first, then an outbound if any SLA windows are affected. Template will be in confluence under /support/gpu-remediation.
ops-bot: Note: capacity-override request #778 opened by raphael. Link: <https://issues.redwood/internal/778|req-778>
raphael: Also adding an autoscale safety margin (15%) to avoid immediate reverts during bursts. Will include metrics to validate margin effectiveness.
nina: Good. Two operational constraints: 1) don't change preemption across more than 20% of hosts at once, 2) schedule kernel restarts only in maintenance windows. Capture both in the runbook.
tom: A heads-up: some legacy hosts (pool-legacy-1) need a manual driver rebind after restart. I'll enumerate hosts and add to the rollout checklist.
zoe: Created JIRA epic GPU-REM-2026 and linked the individual tasks. Will tag owners and add a due-date.
raphael: Posting the circuit-breaker draft in GH: <https://gh.redwood/autoscale/circuit-breaker-draft|cb-draft>
nina: Let's set two async checkpoints: mid-week status (Wed standup) and final sign-off by next Friday. If any owner misses a date, ping the oncall and I'll escalate.
tom: I'll start the canary config today and leave detailed telemetry hooks (per-model tail latency, queue depth, pod eviction rate).
ops-bot: Reminder: maintenance window reserved 2026-04-09 08:00-10:00 UTC.
zoe: Customer outreach plan uploaded: <https://confluence.redwood/gpu-remediation-comms|comms-plan>. Adding CS lead reviewers now.
raphael: After initial canary, we'll run a simulated surge with override active. Please don't run other large experiments in that window.
nina: Noted. Raphael, Tom, Zoe  please update the central follow-up sheet and mark the items DONE when complete. I'll close the loop in next Friday's postmortem follow-up. :white_check_mark:
tom: ack. Starting canary config now.
zoe: ack. Tagging legal for outbound wording review.
raphael: ack. Will update issue #778 with the test plan and rollback steps.
